findings.evidence: "The minimum GPU count for this single-request prefill deadline is four, not eight ... ⌈1.19 PFLOPS ÷ (0.989 × 0.35)⌉ ≈ 4 GPUs meet it"
findings.issue: The phrase "minimum GPU count" is locally scoped as a per-request prefill-feasibility count, but it reads as a deployable GPU-count recommendation. The same paragraph later says the canonical 8-GPU choice is driven by concurrency, KV capacity and headroom, so the two numbers are not alternatives.
findings.fix_instruction: Rename the phrase to "minimum GPU count for this single-request prefill deadline under the stated MFU assumption" and repeat the non-deployability caveat immediately after the arithmetic.

findings.evidence: "Compute the cost on the fleet $/hr ÷ fleet rps basis (5 × $20/hr ÷ 40 rps ≈ ~$0.0007 per request at peak, against 21 × $20/hr ÷ 40 rps ≈ ~$0.0029 at 9.2K input)"
findings.issue: The displayed expression omits the 3,600 s/hr conversion; as written, dividing dollars per hour by requests per second does not yield dollars per request. The intended value is correct only when the hour-to-second conversion is applied.
findings.fix_instruction: Write the full expression with units: "(5 × $20/hr) ÷ (40 rps × 3,600 s/hr) ≈ $0.0007 per request" and similarly for the 21-host case.

findings.evidence: PDF p.90, Canonical Workload box: "TTFT SLO: 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s); p95 ≤ 2 s" and "TPOT SLO: 25 ms/token; p95 ≤ 35 ms". The Preface (PDF p.22) explicitly states: "TTFTmodelled = retrieval + prefill = 1.2 s — a two-term modelled budget, never the TTFT SLO and never TTFTe2e." Table 4-1 on PDF p.84 correctly labels the same values "TTFT budget 1.2 s" and "TPOT budget ~25 ms/token". Section 4.3 on PDF p.102 confirms: "1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to, and any pass/fail judgement on a measured distribution is made against the p95 ceiling, not the budget."
findings.issue: The Canonical Workload box field labels 1.2 s as "TTFT SLO" and 25 ms as "TPOT SLO", directly contradicting the Preface's explicit naming instruction ("never the TTFT SLO"), Table 4-1's correct "TTFT budget" / "TPOT budget" labels (same chapter, same section), and §4.3's statement that pass/fail is judged against the 2 s p95 ceiling, not the 1.2 s budget. A reader consulting only the Canonical Workload box would conclude 1.2 s is the pass/fail SLO threshold, which the book elsewhere says it is not.
findings.fix_instruction: Rename both fields in the Canonical Workload box from "TTFT SLO" to "TTFT budget" and from "TPOT SLO" to "TPOT budget", matching Table 4-1 and §4.3. Alternatively, add a parenthetical like "(design budget; SLO ceiling: p95 ≤ 2 s)" to make the distinction explicit. Scan for other occurrences of "SLO" paired with the 1.2 s / 25 ms budget values rather than the 2 s / 35 ms ceiling values.

findings.chapter: Ch. 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload (§4.6, Memory planning)
findings.evidence: "That 17-slot ceiling is a per-host figure, and its binding limit is per-rank: an 80 GB rank runs 99.97% full at 17.5 slots (Ch 7 §7.3 technical note), so the per-rank test — not this pool-level arithmetic — decides residency." (PDF p. 112, book p. 88)
findings.issue: Dangling cross-reference. Ch 7 §7.3 (PDF pp. 155–171) contains no section or box called a "technical note" and never states the 99.97% figure; its only named notes are "Note on 'does it fit?'" and "Attention-family sensitivity note". A reader who follows the citation to verify the per-rank residency claim (which §4.6 explicitly says "decides residency") finds nothing. The underlying arithmetic is correct (17.5 slots × 3.11296 GB/rank-slot + 17.5 GB weights + 8 GB reserve = 79.98 GB of 80 GB ≈ 99.97%) but the derivation is cited to a target that does not visibly exist.
findings.fix_instruction: Add the per-rank fill computation as an explicitly named "technical note" in Ch 7 §7.3, or repoint the citation to wherever the per-rank 99.97% figure is actually derived.

findings.chapter: Ch. 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload (§4.8 mini-case, Label note)
findings.evidence: "This 5,000-employee growth variant is non-canonical, so its inputs (5,000 employees, 10% peak activity, 50 rps, and the ~8.6 s engine response duration) carry [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]" (PDF p. 115, book p. 91)
findings.issue: Provenance misattribution of an inherited canonical value. The ~8.6 s engine response duration is not an input of the growth variant — it is the canonical W_exec ≈ 8.58 s, derived in Table 4-2 as [canonical scenario][DERIVED] ("Wexec = 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode = 8.58 s, shown as 8.6 s") and reused unchanged in this same mini-case's arithmetic ("50 × 8.6 ≈ 430") and in Ch 6 §6.8. Listing it as an [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] input gives the same quantity two conflicting labels across chapters and leaves ambiguous whether the variant assumes an independent service time.
findings.fix_instruction: State that the variant inherits W_exec ≈ 8.6 s from the canonical scenario (Table 4-2), and restrict the [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] list to the genuinely new inputs (5,000 employees, 10% peak activity, 50 rps).
